claims.text: Sykes–Picot: negotiated Nov 1915–Mar 1916, letter of 16 May 1916; Palestine (less Haifa and Acre) under international administration; contrary to promises to Hussein; revealed by the Bolsheviks in 1917.
King–Crane (June–July 1919, at Wilson's request): 72% of about 1,875 petitions opposed the Zionist programme; advised 'a serious modification of the Zionist immigration program'.
Hope Simpson (30 Aug 1930): almost 30% of Palestinians landless, attributed to Jewish land purchases; incorporated into the Passfield White Paper; reversed by the MacDonald letter.

Peel (7 July 1937): Mandate unworkable; partition, Jewish state on about 20%; exchange of up to 225,000 Arabs and 1,250 Jews; Congress accepted partition as a basis 299–160; Woodhead rejected the plan; Britain dropped partition Nov 1938.
Évian (6–15 July 1938, 32 countries): Palestine kept off the agenda by Britain and the US; Dominican Republic offered up to 100,000; Golda Meir an observer without the right to speak.
Evatt, chairman of the UN Ad Hoc Committee on Palestine (1947), pushed partition to the vote.
